title: Scheduler instrumentation: label prefill vs decode regime and emit selection context
author: Lena Fischer
description:
Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 needs a stable signal for whether a request is currently in prefill or decode (and a consistent notion of “effective context”) so we can: (a) bucket selection decisions by regime, (b) correlate kernel choice with latency and correctness, and (c) avoid guessing based purely on seq_len at the selector boundary. Today the scheduler has the best view of prompt ingestion vs token generation and batching decisions, but we don’t emit a normalized, low-cardinality label downstream.

What this PR does: Adds scheduler-side instrumentation and context propagation to reliably label prefill vs decode for each inference step. Specifically, we introduce a small, versioned “selection context” struct populated by the scheduler and attached to the runtime dispatch call. The context includes: phase={prefill|decode|unknown}, seq_bucket={S|M|L|XL} (based on effective_context_tokens at time of dispatch), effective_context_tokens (int, for logs only), batch_mode={single|microbatch|cont_batch} (bucketed), and a stable request_id. We also emit trace annotations on the scheduler span and a counter/histogram family scoped to the scheduler (not per-model) so we can build selector v2 dashboards without exploding cardinality.

Cardinality controls: phase and seq_bucket are required labels. We explicitly do NOT include prompt_length, exact token counts, model_id, or customer_id as metric labels. Exact counts are only included in debug logs behind sampling (0.1% default; configurable). request_id is only in traces/logs.

Compatibility: The new context is optional at the runtime boundary; if an older runtime is deployed, the scheduler will omit the payload (no behavior change). If an older scheduler is deployed, the runtime selector continues to behave as before (phase=unknown). There is no customer-facing API change.

Testing: Adds unit tests for phase transitions (prefill->decode), boundary cases where the first decode token is emitted in the same scheduler tick, and seq_bucket mapping including off-by-one boundaries. Includes a small integration test in scheduler+runtime harness to verify span attributes and that the context propagates through the dispatch layer.

Rollout: Metrics are behind config flag scheduler.instrumentation.prefill_decode.enabled (default false). Traces attributes are always set but remain low-cardinality. Once enabled, perf-canary will start reporting regime breakdowns for selector v2 (follow-up in ENG-3933).

Notes: This intentionally keeps the regime definition simple: prefill = processing prompt tokens (including cache warmup/prefix ingest); decode = generating new tokens. For multi-turn chat with cached prefixes, a request can start in decode if KV cache hit fully satisfies prefill; we label that as decode (prefill_skipped=true in logs only).

scheduler: emit phase/seq_bucket metrics + trace attributes (low-cardinality)
scheduler: add phase transition tests + bucket boundary tests
runtime interface: accept optional selection context (no-op until selector v2 consumes it)
chore: add config flag + docs for instrumentation sampling
changed_areas: runtime/scheduler: request lifecycle and dispatch boundary
config: scheduler instrumentation flag + sampling rate
tests: scheduler unit tests + scheduler-runtime harness
review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): I like pushing this into scheduler, but I’m worried about defining phase based on “current tick” — we’ve had cases where prefill and first decode token happen back-to-back. Please make sure we don’t mislabel the first decode step as prefill due to buffered events.

Lena Fischer (author): Good call. I updated the phase transition logic to treat “first emitted token” as a hard boundary: any dispatch where generated_tokens>0 is decode, even if prefill tokens were also processed in the same scheduler iteration. Added unit test test_phase_transitions_prefill_to_decode_same_tick.

Grace Kim (review): Can you clarify how effective_context_tokens is computed? Selector v2 needs something consistent across batching modes. Also please do not add exact token counts as metric labels.

Lena Fischer (author): effective_context_tokens = prompt_tokens_consumed + cached_prefix_tokens (if any) at dispatch time; it excludes generated_tokens in decode. Exact counts are only in debug logs. Metrics labels are phase + seq_bucket + batch_mode only.

Thomas Baird (review): Thanks for the cardinality discipline. Two asks: (1) remove batch_mode as a label unless you can justify it; (2) ensure seq_bucket is coarse enough and stable (no per-request bucket edges that depend on heuristics).

Lena Fischer (author): Kept batch_mode but bucketed to {single,microbatch,cont_batch}; this is useful to diagnose outliers where continuous batching changes regime distribution. seq_bucket uses fixed boundaries [0-512]=S, (512-2048]=M, (2048-8192]=L, >8192=XL; boundaries are constants with tests.

Omar El-Sayed (review): On the runtime boundary: please keep the new payload optional and default to “unknown” on missing/older scheduler. Also make sure dispatch structs don’t churn allocations.

Lena Fischer (author): Done — SelectionContext is a small POD passed by pointer; if null, runtime sets phase=unknown and seq_bucket=unknown. No heap alloc on the hot path.

Marcus Reed (review): Can we add a quick integration assertion that the trace attributes show up with expected keys? This will save us time when wiring dashboards.

Lena Fischer (author): Added runtime/integration_tests/test_selection_context_propagation.cc which checks span attrs: redwood.scheduler.phase and redwood.scheduler.seq_bucket.

Grace Kim (approval): Looks good. Please follow up with selector v2 consumption (ENG-3923) once this lands.

Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved after the same-tick fix + tests.

Thomas Baird (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping labels tight.

Merge: Squash merged by Lena Fischer.
release_notes: Internal only: scheduler now can emit prefill/decode regime + seq bucket telemetry (behind scheduler.instrumentation.prefill_decode.enabled). No customer-facing changes.
